To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) muscle actin cDNAs have been identified and characterized and (b) muscle actin genes have been identified and are being studied.
the coding sequences for the contractile muscle proteins are already in the cell in an unexpressing form.
(a) The muscle actin gene family is composed of at least three members.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of gene expression in muscle cells.
the study of muscle cell differentiation and the molecular biology of muscle proteins.
the regulation of muscle differentiation at the molecular level.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
muscle cells contain a set of genes which are expressed at the onset of the differentiation process.
the regulation of gene expression in myogenesis is a complex phenomenon.
muscle cells are already endowed with all the necessary genetic information for the synthesis of muscle specific proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the muscle actin gene is expressed at a low rate in non-muscle cells and that the expression of this gene is regulated at the transcriptional level.
the regulation of muscle genes is not restricted to a single level, but that it is a complex process involving transcription, mRNA splicing and post-transcriptional modification.
the muscle actin gene is present in the genome of non-muscle cells and that its transcription is activated at the onset of muscle cell differentiation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
muscle genes are not expressed in a tissue specific way in the absence of a differentiation process.
muscle actin is expressed in the absence of any detectable transcriptional switch.
the expression of muscle genes is controlled by several levels of regulation.
